title: Maps: find it by its name

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the evening tally here, and try your classes from main.

tasks.title: Count the tickets for each boat
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Counts` with a method `static Map<String, Integer> byBoat(List<String> tickets)`. Each ticket is the name of a boat. It gives back a new map from each boat on the list to the number of its tickets. `tickets` stays as it is.

Check calls `byBoat` with lists of tickets of its own, made with `List.of`: several boats, boats with one ticket each, one boat many times, and no tickets at all. It compares the map that comes back with the right tally as maps, whatever order the keys are in.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about a key that is not there, and about counting with a map.
Make a new, empty map in the method.
For each ticket, read the boat's count so far, and put back one more.
Give the map back, and print it from main.
hints: The first ticket of each boat finds no count in the map yet. Decide what the count is then, before you add one to it.
Putting a value under a key writes over the one it had, so read the old count first. A missing key can be asked about, or given a value of your own.

tasks.title: Write the tally in the order of the boats' names
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Report` with a method `static List<String> lines(Map<String, Integer> counts)`. It gives back one line per boat, as in `Gannet: 3`, in alphabetical order of the boats' names, whatever order the map keeps them in. `counts` stays as it is.

Check hands `lines` maps of its own: a `HashMap` and a `LinkedHashMap` whose boats were put in so that the order each keeps differs from alphabetical order, a map of one boat, and an empty one. It reads every line in order, and the map afterwards to see it has not changed.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about walking a map and keeping it in order.
Make a map that keeps its keys sorted, from counts.
Walk its entries, and add a line for each to a new list.
hints: A HashMap keeps its keys in an order of its own, and the task asks for alphabetical order. Some maps keep their keys sorted.
A sorted map made from counts leaves counts as it is. Each entry has the key and the value the line needs.
The loop: `for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry : new TreeMap<>(counts).entrySet()) { lines.add(entry.getKey() + ": " + entry.getValue()); }`.

tasks.title: Look up the seats left on a sailing
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a record `Sailing` with a `String boat` and an `int hour`, in that order: a record is equal to any other with the same parts, as a key must be, with nothing more to write. Then write a class `Seats` with a method `static int left(Map<Sailing, Integer> booked, Sailing sailing, int capacity)`: the capacity less the places booked on that sailing. A sailing with nothing booked is not in the map at all, and has every seat left.

Check makes a map of its own with sailings it makes, then asks `left` about new `Sailing` objects that hold the same boat and hour, as a sailing read in would be: one that is booked, one that is not, another boat at a booked hour, a full one, and another capacity. It also checks that `Sailing` is a record and reads its parts.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about a key needing equals and hashCode.
Write the record: its parts go in the round brackets after its name.
Write left: look up the places booked on the sailing, with 0 for one that is not in the map.
Give back the capacity less those places.
hints: Check looks a sailing up with a new object, so the map has to find a key that is equal, not the very same one. A record is equal by its parts.
A sailing with nothing booked is not a key in the map, and looking it up gives back null. Ask whether the key is there, or give the map a value of your own for a missing key.
The record is `record Sailing(String boat, int hour) { }`, and left is `return capacity - booked.getOrDefault(sailing, 0);`.
